messages.subject_clean: [seewave] how do I reduce the file sizes produced when saving spectro() figures as tiff/pdf/eps?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Yes vector format (eps and pdf) should be avoided for a spectrogram. You may need to convince the publisher...

I usually use the png raster format: it is a free, open, light and lossless format.

The following parameters usaully provide nice results:

data(tico)
png("tico.png", width=1200, height=1200, point=20)
spectro(tico, ovlp=85)
dev.off()

png("tico_res300.png", point=12, width=3000, height=3000, res=300)
spectro(tico, ovlp=85)
dev.off()

HTH

Jerome

The oscillo() function does not have an y-axis unit as, as you suggested, the input can vary on any range depending on the source file format. In most cases, it is therefore better to think this axis as a relative amplitude scale without unit.

HTH

Thanks very much,

James

filtered = ffilter(sound0, from=0, to=freq/2)
